newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares boosted after economic reports.
newsitem.headline: German shares boosted after economic reports.

text.p: The outlook for German shares brightened after a pair of economic reports showed inflation remained little threat and the economy was gaining steam.
The IBIS DAX index was up 18.31 points in morning trade at 3,618.71, after jumping to a new high in early dealings.
The Ifo economic research institute said its April west German business climate index jumped to 94.7 from 92.6, higher than expected.
The Bundesbank announced that M3 money supply grew an annualised 6.7 percent in April versus the average for the fourth quarter of 1996, lower than expectations.

Building group Philipp Holzmann AG was up three marks to 473.00 after reporting that it returned to profit last year with a one million mark profit, rebounding from a 443 million mark loss the year before.

Utilities group Bewag AG, meanwhile, said nine-month pre-tax profit climbed to 359 million marks from 372 million marks during the same period a year earlier. The company also said it expected 1996/97 profit of between 170 million and 180 million marks compared with 169 million marks a year ago.
